description: Design a simple state machine that simulates a robot moving in a grid. The robot can be in one of four states: Moving Up, Moving Down, Moving Left, and Moving Right. The state transitions are controlled by a 2-bit input that indicates the desired direction: 00 for Up, 01 for Down, 10 for Left, and 11 for Right. The output should be the current state of the robot in binary format.
code:
module robot_movement(  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input [1:0] direction,  
    output reg [1:0] state  
);  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset)  
            state <= 2'b00; // Initial state (Moving Up)  
        else begin  
            case (direction)  
                2'b00: state <= 2'b00; // Moving Up  
                2'b01: state <= 2'b01; // Moving Down  
                2'b10: state <= 2'b10; // Moving Left  
                2'b11: state <= 2'b11; // Moving Right  
                default: state <= state; // Retain current state  
            endcase  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [1:0] workload, // Workload input (00: low, 01: medium, 10: high, 11: very high)

    output reg [1:0] voltage // Voltage output (00: 1.0V, 01: 1.2V, 10: 1.4V, 11: 1.6V)
);

        if (reset) begin
            frequency <= 2'b00;
            voltage <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            case (workload)
                2'b00: begin
                    frequency <= 2'b00; // 0Hz
                    voltage <= 2'b00; // 1.0V
                end
                2'b01: begin
                    frequency <= 2'b01; // 1Hz
                    voltage <= 2'b01; // 1.2V
                end
                2'b10: begin
                    frequency <= 2'b10; // 2Hz
                    voltage <= 2'b10; // 1.4V
                end
                2'b11: begin
                    frequency <= 2'b11; // 3Hz
                    voltage <= 2'b11; // 1.6V
                end
                default: begin
                    frequency <= 2'b00; // Default to 0Hz
                    voltage <= 2'b00; // Default to 1.0V
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

);

description: Design a Viterbi decoder that takes a sequence of input bits and outputs the decoded bits. The decoder will use a simple 2-state trellis and will be provided with a known state transition and output mapping.
code:
module viterbi_decoder(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [1:0] input_bits,
    output reg [1:0] decoded_bits
);
    reg [1:0] current_state, next_state;

    // State transition logic
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            current_state <= 2'b00;
            decoded_bits <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            current_state <= next_state;
        end
    end

    // Next state logic
    always @(*) begin
        case (current_state)
            2'b00: begin
                if (input_bits == 2'b00) begin
                    next_state = 2'b00;
                    decoded_bits = 2'b00; // Output for state 00
                end else begin
                    next_state = 2'b01;
                    decoded_bits = 2'b01; // Output for state 01
                end
            end
            2'b01: begin
                if (input_bits == 2'b00) begin
                    next_state = 2'b10;
                    decoded_bits = 2'b10; // Output for state 10
                end else begin
                    next_state = 2'b11;
                    decoded_bits = 2'b11; // Output for state 11
                end
            end
            2'b10: begin
                if (input_bits == 2'b00) begin
                    next_state = 2'b00;
                    decoded_bits = 2'b00; // Output for state 00
                end else begin
                    next_state = 2'b01;
                    decoded_bits = 2'b01; // Output for state 01
                end
            end
            2'b11: begin
                if (input_bits == 2'b00) begin
                    next_state = 2'b10;
                    decoded_bits = 2'b10; // Output for state 10
                end else begin
                    next_state = 2'b11;
                    decoded_bits = 2'b11; // Output for state 11
                end
            end
            default: begin
                next_state = 2'b00;
                decoded_bits = 2'b00;
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

    input clk,
    input reset,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: RED, 01: GREEN, 10: YELLOW
);

    reg [1:0] next_state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Start from RED state
            timer <= 3'b000;
        end else begin
            // Update state based on timer
            if (timer == 3'b111) begin // Timer expires
                state <= next_state;
                timer <= 3'b000; // Reset timer
            end else begin
                timer <= timer + 1; // Increment timer
            end
        end
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            2'b00: next_state = 2'b01; // RED to GREEN
            2'b01: next_state = 2'b10; // GREEN to YELLOW
            2'b10: next_state = 2'b00; // YELLOW to RED

        endcase
    end
endmodule

    input reset,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    input data_valid,

    output reg last_packet
);

    reg [31:0] packet_buffer; // Buffer to hold the current packet

        if (reset) begin
            byte_count <= 0;
            last_packet <= 0;
            packet_buffer <= 0;
        end else if (data_valid) begin
            packet_buffer <= {packet_buffer[23:0], data_in}; // Shift in new data

                packet_out <= packet_buffer[31:24]; // Output the packet
                last_packet <= 1; // Indicate last packet
                byte_count <= 0; // Reset byte count
                packet_buffer <= 0; // Clear buffer

        end
    end
endmodule

module kalman_filter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [15:0] measurement,
    output reg [15:0] position,
    output reg [15:0] velocity
);
    reg [15:0] state [0:1]; // state[0] = position, state[1] = velocity
    reg [15:0] P[0:1][0:1]; // state covariance matrix
    reg [15:0] Q; // process noise covariance
    reg [15:0] R; // measurement noise covariance
    reg [15:0] K; // Kalman gain

    initial begin
        state[0] = 0; // initial position
        state[1] = 0; // initial velocity
        P[0][0] = 1000; P[0][1] = 0; // initial covariance
        P[1][0] = 0; P[1][1] = 1000;
        Q = 1; // process noise
        R = 100; // measurement noise
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state[0] <= 0;
            state[1] <= 0;
        end else begin
            // Prediction step
            state[0] <= state[0] + state[1]; // x' = x + v
            P[0][0] <= P[0][0] + Q; // update covariance

            // Measurement update step
            K <= P[0][0] / (P[0][0] + R); // Kalman gain
            state[0] <= state[0] + K * (measurement - state[0]); // update position
            state[1] <= state[1]; // velocity remains the same
            P[0][0] <= (1 - K) * P[0][0]; // update covariance
            P[0][1] <= (1 - K) * P[0][1];
            P[1][0] <= (1 - K) * P[1][0];
            P[1][1] <= P[1][1] + Q; // update velocity covariance

            position <= state[0];
            velocity <= state[1];
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a UART transmitter that takes an 8-bit data input, a send signal, and transmits the data serially at a specified baud rate. The transmitter should include start and stop bits, and the transmission should be controlled by a clock signal. The module should also have an output signal indicating when the transmission is complete.
code:
module uart_transmitter (
    input wire clk,           // System clock
    input wire reset,         // Reset signal
    input wire [7:0] data_in, // 8-bit data input
    input wire send,          // Send signal
    output reg tx,           // Transmitter output
    output reg busy          // Busy signal indicating transmission in progress
);

    reg [3:0] bit_count;     // Bit counter
    reg [9:0] shift_reg;     // Shift register to store data with start and stop bits
    reg [15:0] baud_count;    // Baud rate counter
    parameter BAUD_RATE = 16'd104; // Adjust this for desired baud rate

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            tx <= 1;               // Idle state is high
            busy <= 0;
            bit_count <= 0;
            baud_count <= 0;
        end else if (send && !busy) begin
            busy <= 1;             // Set busy flag
            shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Load data with stop and start bits
            bit_count <= 0;
            baud_count <= 0;
        end else if (busy) begin
            baud_count <= baud_count + 1;
            if (baud_count == BAUD_RATE) begin
                baud_count <= 0;
                tx <= shift_reg[bit_count]; // Transmit current bit
                if (bit_count < 10) begin
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Move to the next bit
                end else begin
                    busy <= 0; // Transmission complete
                    tx <= 1;   // Set to idle state
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description:

    output reg [15:0] data_out
);

        if (rst) begin
            state <= 0;
            transfer_complete <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: if (start) begin
                    state <= 1;
                end
                1: begin
                    data_out <= data_in; // Transfer data
                    transfer_complete <= 1; // Set transfer complete
                    state <= 2; // Move to next state

            if (clk_a == clk_b) 
                state <= 2'b01; // in-phase
            else if (clk_a) 
                state <= 2'b10; // leading
            else 
                state <= 2'b00; // lagging
        end
    end

    always @(state) begin
        case(state)
            2'b00: phase_out = 0; // lagging
            2'b01: phase_out = 1; // in-phase

    input wire reset,
    input wire [15:0] z_measured,  // Measured position
    input wire [15:0] v_prev,      // Previous velocity estimate
    input wire [15:0] x_prev,      // Previous position estimate
    input wire [15:0] dt,          // Time step
    output reg [15:0] x_est,       // Updated position estimate
    output reg [15:0] v_est        // Updated velocity estimate
);

    reg [15:0] r = 16'd10; // Measurement noise covariance

The division should occur on the rising edge of the clock, and the circuit should be able to handle division by zero by outputting the maximum value for both quotient and remainder.
code:
module divider (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [3:0] dividend,
    input [3:0] divisor,
    output reg [3:0] quotient,
    output reg [3:0] remainder
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            quotient <= 4'b0000;
            remainder <= 4'b0000;
        end else if (divisor != 4'b0000) begin
            quotient <= dividend / divisor;
            remainder <= dividend % divisor;
        end else begin
            quotient <= 4'b1111; // Max value for 4-bits
            remainder <= 4'b1111; // Max value for 4-bits
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit barrel shifter that can perform left and right shifts. The barrel shifter should accept a 8-bit input data and a 3-bit shift amount. The output should be the data shifted left or right based on a mode signal: '0' for left shift and '1' for right shift.

);

description: Design a simple fan speed control system that has a 2-bit input representing the temperature level (00 for low, 01 for medium, 10 for high, 11 for off) and a 1-bit output for the fan speed control. Create a fixed-priority arbiter that gives access to a shared resource based on the priority of the requests. The arbiter should have 4 request lines (req[3:0]) and one grant line (grant[3:0]). The highest priority will be granted first.
code:
module fixed_priority_arbiter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] req,
    output reg [3:0] grant
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            grant <= 4'b0000;
        end else begin
            grant <= 4'b0000; // Default to no grant
            if (req[0]) grant[0] <= 1'b1; // Grant to highest priority
            else if (req[1]) grant[1] <= 1'b1; // Grant to second highest priority
            else if (req[2]) grant[2] <= 1'b1; // Grant to third highest priority
            else if (req[3]) grant[3] <= 1'b1; // Grant to lowest priority
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Serial-in Parallel-out (SIPO) shift register that takes a serial input and outputs the data in parallel form. It should have a clock input, a reset input, and an enable input. When enabled, it shifts in the serial data on each clock edge. The output should be available after a specified number of clock cycles, corresponding to the width of the shift register.

);

    end else if (enable) begin

always @(posedge clk) begin
    parallel_out <= shift_reg; // Output parallel data
end

endmodule

description: Design a simple packet filtering firewall using Verilog. The firewall will filter packets based on a predefined set of rules. Design a simple memory allocator with a fixed-size memory block. The allocator should have a request input for memory allocation and a free input to release the memory. The output should indicate whether the allocation was successful or not. The memory block size is fixed at 8 bytes, and the allocator should handle multiple requests and free operations correctly.
code:
module memory_allocator(  
    input wire clk,  
    input wire reset,  
    input wire request,  
    input wire free,  
    output reg success  
);  
    reg [3:0] mem_usage; // 4 bits to represent usage from 0 to 15 (4 bytes)  
    parameter MAX_MEMORY = 8; // Maximum memory in bytes  

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            mem_usage <= 0;  
            success <= 0;  
        end else begin  
            if (request) begin  
                if (mem_usage < MAX_MEMORY) begin  
                    mem_usage <= mem_usage + 1;  
                    success <= 1; // Allocation successful  
                end else begin  
                    success <= 0; // Allocation failed  
                end  
            end else if (free) begin  
                if (mem_usage > 0) begin  
                    mem_usage <= mem_usage - 1;  
                    success <= 1; // Free successful  
                end else begin  
                    success <= 0; // Nothing to free  
                end  
            end  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description:
Design a combinational logic circuit in Verilog that computes the value of a polynomial given by the equation:
P(x) = a3*x^3 + a2*x^2 + a1*x + a0
where a3, a2, a1, and a0 are the coefficients of the polynomial and x is the input variable. The circuit should take 4 coefficients and a single input x, and output the result of the polynomial evaluation.
code:
module polynomial_evaluation (
    input [3:0] a3, a2, a1, a0, // Coefficients of the polynomial
    input [3:0] x,              // Input variable
    output [7:0] P              // Output of the polynomial
);
    wire [7:0] x2, x3, term1, term2, term3, term4;

    assign x2 = x * x;         // x^2
    assign x3 = x2 * x;        // x^3

    assign term1 = a3 * x3;    // a3 * x^3
    assign term2 = a2 * x2;    // a2 * x^2
    assign term3 = a1 * x;      // a1 * x
    assign term4 = a0;          // a0

    assign P = term1 + term2 + term3 + term4; // P(x) = a3*x^3 + a2*x^2 + a1*x + a0
endmodule

description: Design a 4-bit Serial-in Serial-out (SISO) shift register. The shift register should take a serial input and shift it through the 4 bits. It should have a clock input and a reset input. On each clock cycle, if the reset is not asserted, the new bit should be shifted in and the oldest bit should be outputted. After 4 clock cycles, the output should reflect the last 4 bits that were shifted in.
code:
module siso_shift_register (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input serial_in,
    output reg [3:0] parallel_out,
    output reg serial_out
);

            parallel_out <= 4'b0000;
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            serial_out <= parallel_out[0]; // Output the oldest bit

        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 5-bit ring counter in Verilog. The ring counter should have a single input clock signal and a reset signal. When the reset is activated, the counter should be set to a predefined state (for example, 00001). On each rising edge of the clock, the counter should shift left, with the leftmost bit going to the rightmost position. The output of the counter should be available as a 5-bit output.

);

Design a voltage and frequency scaling controller that adjusts the operating frequency of a system based on a 2-bit voltage level input. description:

2. An input data signal (`data_in`) that is only relevant when in input mode.

4. A clock signal (`clk`) that allows for synchronous operation.
5. A reset signal (`reset`) that initializes the controller.
The GPIO controller should store the input data when in input mode and drive the output data when in output mode.
code:
module gpio_controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire mode,         // 0 for input mode, 1 for output mode

    output reg [7:0] data_out
);

        if (reset) begin
            data_out <= 8'b00000000;  // Reset output data
        end else begin
            if (mode) begin
                data_out <= data_in;   // Output mode: reflect input data

description:

Design a Verilog module that implements a simple Kalman filter for sensor fusion. The module should take in noisy measurements from two sensors and output a filtered estimate of the true state. The Kalman filter should maintain its state across clock cycles and have the following inputs: 
- Measurement from sensor 1 (input1), 
- Measurement from sensor 2 (input2), 
- Control input (control),
- Clock (clk),
- Reset (reset).

The output should be the estimated state (output_estimate). The filter should also include parameters for the process noise covariance (Q) and measurement noise covariance (R), which can be set as parameters in the module.
code:
module KalmanFilter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire signed [15:0] input1,
    input wire signed [15:0] input2,
    input wire signed [15:0] control,
    output reg signed [15:0] output_estimate
);
    parameter signed [15:0] Q = 16'h0001; // Process noise covariance
    parameter signed [15:0] R = 16'h0005; // Measurement noise covariance
    reg signed [15:0] x_hat; // Estimated state
    reg signed [15:0] P; // Estimate uncertainty
    reg signed [15:0] K; // Kalman gain

    // Initialization
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            x_hat <= 16'h0000; // Initial estimate
            P <= 16'h0001; // Initial uncertainty
        end else begin
            // Prediction step
            x_hat <= x_hat + control; // Predicted state
            P <= P + Q; // Predicted uncertainty

            // Measurement update
            K <= P / (P + R); // Kalman gain
            x_hat <= x_hat + K * (input1 + input2) / 2 - x_hat; // Update estimate
            P <= (1 - K) * P; // Update uncertainty
            
            // Output the estimate
            output_estimate <= x_hat;
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire rst,  
    input wire serial_in,
